posts.title: Draft invoice fields for human review
posts.promise: Extract invoice details into a review sheet; a person checks every amount.
posts.whatItIs: A small proposed service would take an operator supplied invoice PDF and draft selected fields, such as invoice number, amount and due date, into a review sheet. A public workflow listing describes monitoring a Drive folder, extracting invoice fields and logging them in Google Sheets. That supports a prototype direction, not a tested service or accounting accuracy. The paid administrator notice names invoicing, customer follow-up, time reporting and reporting key figures to an owner. It does not say anyone wants an AI tool.
posts.whoPays: Hypothesis: a small professional office might pay for help preparing invoice records; neither this buyer nor willingness to pay is established.
loop: An operator places a fictional invoice PDF in a test folder.
The workflow extracts chosen fields into a draft row.
It records the source filename and marks missing fields.
A person checks the invoice against the draft.
The person corrects it and decides whether any record should be entered elsewhere.
posts.evidence: The paid notice establishes human invoicing and reporting work. The n8n listing describes PDF invoice extraction and Google Sheets logging. Neither source demonstrates this proposed service, its accuracy, customers or revenue.
posts.uncertainty: Fields and the test folder are proposed design choices. The public listing is a workflow description, not evidence of testing or outcomes. Use fictional PDFs only for the prototype; real deployment would need permission, system access and privacy review, and a person must approve financial records.
first24Hours: Create three fictional invoice PDFs with varied layouts.
Build a sheet with invoice number, amount, due date and a source filename column.
Compare drafted fields against each PDF and record every error for human review.
